evidence.note: Sized model (~30M) to H100 hardware and checked data/template before training; did quick py_compile checks — cheap validation of feasibility, but did NOT cheaply validate the quantized-checkpoint loading path before committing to a long run.
Verified checkpoint size (28.4MB) at first validation (step 250), reserving cheap compute to confirm the size-cap contract before letting the long run proceed.

Interrupted the 30M run at step 4000 with explicit extrapolation reasoning that it wouldn't cross target, then scaled to 53.8M and compared trajectories at matching steps — genuine payoff-based reallocation as results came in.

Only after two full 10k-step runs discovered q4 checkpoint degrades bpb 0.970→1.008; a cheap early probe of the quantization/loading contract would have prevented this expensive late surprise — a budget-allocation miss.

Spent a very large share of budget on sprawling quantization searches (q4/q5/q6/q7, NF4, lzma, repeated fine-tunes) plus many wasted interrupt attempts (96-140) — exhaustive, mostly unproductive tuning rather than targeted allocation.

reasoning: The agent goes beyond level 3 by comparing expected payoff (extrapolating validation curves to decide the 30M→53M scale-up and comparing runs at matching steps) and clearly meets level 5 (early size/contract size checks, roughly sized runs, adaptive re-sizing). It does not reach level 8: it never ran a small informative probe to estimate the steps/capacity needed, failed to cheaply validate the decisive quantization-loading contract before spending two full training runs, and then poured a disproportionate, unbudgeted share of compute into an exhaustive terminal quantization search and repeated failed interrupts. This places it between the level-5 and level-8 anchors, at 6.
